newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: DKLS down on Cambodia woes - analysts.
newsitem.headline: DKLS down on Cambodia woes - analysts.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian building and construction company DKLS Industries Bhd fell on Monday on fears that fighting on the streets of Phnom Penh may affect its interests in Cambodia, analysts said.
At the midday break, DKLS shares lost 40 cents to 10.40 ringgit.
"DKLS has been awarded a highway project in Cambodia. It's possibly one reason for the fall in its share price," said Ooi Soon Beng, head of research at Inter-Pacific Securities.
DKLS announced earlier in July that it planned to subscribe for 60 percent of the equity of Phnom Penh Highways Co Ltd (PPH). PPH has a paid-up capital of $2.5 million.
PPH had entered into a contract with the Cambodian government to build a road from the Chom Chao to Stung Mean Chey in Cambodia, and to collect tolls from its users for 20 years.

At least 12 people were killed and over 50 were wounded in a weekend of fighting on the streets of Phnom Penh as troops loyal to the country's two rival prime ministers fought for control of the city.
